summary: hex-encode-utils postinstall exfiltrates host identifiers and fetch-decrypt-executes a remote Python payload
details: Package advertised as a hex encoding utility ships a postinstall runtime.js that, gated only by a developer-machine heuristic (presence of Desktop/Documents/Downloads), POSTs installer identifiers (os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, os.platform(), node version, OS release, package version) to https://steel-mere-4155.ricardorichp.workers.dev/report. It then fetches an opaque blob from the same host at /e, AES-256-GCM-decrypts it using a key derived from a hardcoded seed string (labeled as a 'BIP-0174 PSBT' constant), writes the resulting Python to ~/.cache/hex-encode-utils/modules/, and spawns python3 detached with stdio ignored via unref() so it outlives the npm install. TLS certificate verification is disabled (rejectUnauthorized: false) on both the exfil POST and the payload GET, and comments frame the behavior as 'standard telemetry' and a 'runtime integrity module' comparable to Next.js/Nuxt/Angular CLI. The purpose (hex encoding) does not require host reconnaissance, encrypted remote payload delivery, or detached Python execution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
